questions.question: Given your experience with Go, explain how you would design a scalable, fault-tolerant solution for a high-traffic Principal Distributed Systems Architect workload. What trade-offs do you consider?
questions.candidateAnswer: I have designed scalable distributed key-value stores in Go using Raft consensus for state machine replication, PostgreSQL for cold metadata storage, and Redis for caching to achieve sub-millisecond read latency.
questions.feedback: Adequate surface-level answer, but lacked deeper technical depth, specific metrics, or practical implementation steps. Strengths: Successfully referenced relevant concepts: go, latency, caching. Improvement: Elaborate further on architectural trade-offs and edge cases. Could have addressed: scalability, concurrency, fault tolerance.
